thread:
maria.g: FYI ACME reported missing inference audit lines in their private VPC since ~11:30 UTC. Control plane shows request accepted but dataplane sink has gaps. They also see spikes of 429s and duplicated ingestion leading to billing blips.

aj: Can you paste the minimal repro logs they sent? 429s might be our rate limiter or the customer NAT choking.

maria.g: here are snippets (redacted):
```
2026-03-16T11:29:45Z control-plane INFO request received tenant=acme req_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-16T11:29:46Z dataplane WARN deliver failed sink=audit-s3 err=connection-reset
2026-03-16T11:29:46Z dataplane RETRY attempt=1 req_id=abc123 err=timeout
2026-03-16T11:29:47Z dataplane INFO deliver ok req_id=abc123
2026-03-16T11:30:12Z dataplane INFO deliver ok req_id=def456
2026-03-16T11:31:01Z dataplane MISSING req_id=ghi789 // expected but not present in sink
```

samir: Two things jump out: (1) intermittent connection resets to the audit sink (S3 proxy in their VPC) and (2) retries — duplicates could cause billing anomalies. Could be NAT port exhaustion or firewall silently dropping long-lived connections. Also check KMS/HSM handshake logs: if wrap/unwarp errors happen we may retry payloads.

aj: do we have KMS errors? maria, paste any dataplane error lines around 11:31.

maria.g: here's the relevant KMS-ish trace from their host agent: `wrap_key failed: TLS handshake timeout` and `crypto: remote error: handshake failure`. No 403s from our control plane, just timeouts between their host and kms.company.internal (customer-managed HSM).

infra-luke: This sounds like a dataplane -> HSM path problem inside their VPC. Common culprits: stateful firewall with aggressive conntrack timeout, port-preserving NAT limits, or a proxy doing deep-inspection and dropping TLS after N seconds. Ask the customer for: conntrack counters, NAT ephemeral port range, and firewall idle timeout.

maria.g: I asked them for `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` and `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` and their cloud firewall policy. Waiting on reply.

support-ops: They replied with numbers: conntrack_count=120k, conntrack_max=131072, port_range=32768 60999, firewall idle timeout=30s. They also run an egress proxy that rewrites SNI.

samir: 30s idle timeout is very low for long-lived TLS sessions (HSM handshakes + keepalives). If a sidecar or proxy closes the TCP before we finish KV cache exchanges we'll get handshake failures. Suggest setting firewall idle to >=300s and increasing conntrack_max to 250k. Also ensure NAT port range is large enough — their port range ~28k is okay but with many ephemeral flows and NAT it might be tight if port reuse is high.

aj: Can we provide a short repro they can run to demonstrate the break? Something non-invasive.

samir: Ask them to run a looped curl that preserves connections and prints status, e.g.:
```
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -H "X-Tenant: acme" https://dataplane.internal/v1/audit/ping || echo "fail $i"
  sleep 0.1
done
```
This will exercise connection reuse and surface resets quickly. Also ask them to run `sudo conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` during the test.

maria.g: sent commands and asked them to capture tcpdump on the host with: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host kms.company.internal and tcp -w /tmp/kms.pcap`.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-ACME-AUDIT-LOSS (priority=P2) by maria.g

infra-luke: While waiting for repro, mitigation options: (A) enable buffered audit delivery (local disk ephemeral buffer) so transient egress drops don't drop events; (B) switch their sink to our hosted audit-relay temporarily (with customer approval) so we stop stressing their egress; (C) tune keepalive/idle timeouts on the agent to force TCP keepalives every 20s.

support-ops: customer prefers (A) + (C) initially. They've agreed to a maintenance window in 30m to change firewall idle timeout. They will also run the curl loop and provide tcpdump.

samir: Also note: if HSM wrap fails intermittently and we retry the full payload later, that can explain duplicates and billing spikes. Add idempotency keys per-audit-event on our ingest path to dedupe within a short window — open a follow-up ticket to product.

aj: Thanks — assign to infra-luke for firewall guidance and to support-ops for coordinating with the customer. Recording next steps:
- infra-luke: recommend firewall idle >=300s and conntrack_max -> 250k + watch counters
- support-ops: run curl loop + tcpdump, share pcap
- maria.g: enable local audit buffering on agent v1.12 for ACME in the meantime

infra-luke: I'll prepare the exact iptables/sysctl snippets:
```
# increase conntrack
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=250000
# tcp keepalive
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60
# agent side: set keepalive to 20s in /etc/redwood/agent.conf
audit_buffering.enabled=true
audit_buffering.max_disk_mb=500
```

maria.g: customer ran the curl loop and tcpdump. They saw `RST` from proxy to HSM after ~28s and a flurry of retries. pcap attached to ticket.

support-ops: Customer applied firewall change to 300s and increased conntrack. They said duplicates dropped after ~2 minutes. Billing spike reduced.

samir: mark this triage as resolved once we confirm 24h of stable delivery and ask product for dedupe window. Also recommend we add a KB article for "Private VPC audit delivery troubleshooting" with the above checks.

maria.g: 👍 closing here after 24h stable. Thanks all :tada:
